id: HL-07 a section holding an indented fence line or a fence in a blockquote is left as written (0.1.5 E-3 review round 6; 0.1.6 D-71)
note: 0.1.5 E-3 review round 6. fence_lines closed a block on a closing line at any indent, so a "    ```" line inside a ``` block (content, as CommonMark reads it) ended it, and it did not see a fence after a blockquote marker; in both a range inside the block was listed and published, where 0.1.4 refused it. A closing line is now indented at most 3 columns (or as far as the opening line, for a fence in a list item), and fences are read after `>` markers; a block in a quote ends with the quote. 0.1.6 D-71: fix() and move_lines rewrite nothing in a section (a ## heading to the next) that holds a line with a run of 3 or more backticks or tildes, a blockquote line or a line indented 4 or more columns that is not a list continuation; such a section keeps 0.1.4 behaviour (the lint blocks, the draft is kept), so no code block is guessed at. Step 1: the plain range beside the blocks now blocks too; step 2: a fence that closes (in a list item, in a quote) still leaves its section as written.
